lessonRef.unitTitle: PF5 — Financial Investing: Long-Horizon Investing as an Adult
lessonRef.title: Unit performance task: a written rule for market declines

focus: a written rule for market declines
objective: Assemble the figures a fictional decline policy has to be built on — the fall, the recovery required, continued contributions, and the fee charged throughout — and write the policy.
scenario: The fictional balance, contribution, fee, and decline below are invented for this exercise. The decline is a scenario for planning purposes and is not a forecast.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional account figures in these directions

tasks.directions: A fictional account holds $31,500, receives $340 a month, and is charged an annual fee of 0.22% of the balance. Plan for a scenario in which the balance falls 28%.

prompts.text: What is the balance after a 28% fall?
What gain on the reduced balance would restore $31,500, to two decimal places?
What is the annual fee at the reduced balance?

tasks.directions: Now carry the account forward through 18 months of continued contributions.

prompts.text: Ignoring any further movement in the balance, what does the account hold after those contributions?
What is the annual fee at that balance?
By how much has the annual fee risen?

tasks.directions: Put the fee in the terms the policy will have to justify.

prompts.text: What proportion of the 18 months of contributions does one year of the fee represent, to two decimal places?

tasks.directions: Write the policy. Attach a figure to each part of it.

prompts.text: Write the decline policy this fictional investor should set down now, before any fall occurs. Cover what happens to contributions, what would and would not count as a reason to sell, and how the policy handles anyone who contacts the investor during a decline offering to help. State plainly what your policy cannot guarantee.

remediation: If the required gain comes out as 28%, it is being measured against the original $31,500 rather than the $22,680.00 that remains. The $8,820.00 has to be regained from the reduced balance, which needs 38.89%. The same asymmetry applies to every decline: the recovery percentage always exceeds the fall percentage.
extension: Recompute the balance, the required gain, and the fee after a 45% fall instead, and say what the two cases together show about how quickly the required recovery grows.
